packages.label: מַחֲלֹקֶת וּמוֹת הָרוּחָנִי
packages.reason: The teaching's single bechina equates the talmudic principle 'אֵין אָדָם מֵת וַחֲצִי' (no person dies halfway — i.e., one either attains full spiritual continuity or is fully cut off) with machloket (strife, controversy). The logic is that machloket IS the mode of dying in full — it erases one's name from the tradition entirely. David's request to 'dwell in Your tent forever' is fulfilled through disciples quoting halachah in one's name; machloket prevents this, reducing a sage to the anonymous labels 'אחרים' or 'יש אומרים'. Both nodes — the rabbinic death-principle and machloket — share the same essential nature: the domain of complete severance from life and continuity. This is unambiguously an evil package: machloket belongs to the side of the sitra achra (as confirmed by Torah #277 in the same dataset, where 'סטרא אחרא הוא בחינת מחלקת'). The talmudic phrase 'אין אדם מת וחצי' is invoked here in its dark corollary — when machloket is present, there is no 'halfway' reprieve; the result is complete obliteration from the chain of tradition.
